confirmed.title: First tap on a re-enabled guest chip is silently swallowed when it directly follows editing a player name field
repro: Fresh page: New game, name two rows Ava and Ben, Skip photo on both, Shuffle & start, tap the pass screen, then menu -> Home (Ava and Ben are now 'Played before' people)
New game again - roster prefills Ava/Ben, both chips grey 'already playing'
Tap into row 2's name field and type 'Cara' over 'Ben', leaving the caret in the field (do not tap elsewhere first)
The Ben chip lights up as addable; tap it exactly once
confirmed.expected: Ben is seated on the roster and his chip greys to 'already playing' (with the 'Ben added.' announcement)
confirmed.actual: Nothing happens: no row added, chip stays enabled, no announcement; a second tap on the same chip seats Ben normally. Mechanism per report: onInput's change branch calls paintPeople(), which replaceChildren()-rebuilds every chip on the blur caused by the tap's own mousedown, so the composed click retargets to #people-list and matches no [data-action].
sources: roster:First tap on a guest chip is silently swallowed when it directly follows editing a player name
confirmed.rationale: Single report (its two variants - rename and clear-name - share the same replaceChildren-on-blur root cause, so one cluster). Not by-design. Rubric fit is S3 'janky-but-recoverable flow': the tap is silently dead but the chip visibly stays enabled and a second tap works, so no feature is outright broken (S2 would require that) and no player is irreversibly lost from the roster. Reporter's S3 stands.

v1.reason: Reproduced first try on the live site with a fresh browser session following the repro verbatim (script: scratch/qa/round-5/verify-roster-chip-first-tap-swallowed-after-edit-1/verify.mjs, screenshots 01-05). After typing 'Cara' over 'Ben' with the caret left in the field, the re-enabled Ben chip's first tap did nothing: roster stayed [Ava, Cara], chip stayed enabled, and #live-status kept stale text (no 'Ben added.'). A second tap on the same chip seated Ben and announced 'Ben added.' — that second tap also serves as the control (field already blurred, single tap works), proving the swallow is specific to the tap-directly-after-edit sequence. Mechanism confirmed in public/music/ui.js: onInput handles the blur-fired 'change' and calls paintPeople() (line 4528), which replaceChildren-rebuilds every chip (lines 875/921) between the tap's mousedown and mouseup, so the composed click retargets above any [data-action]. No console/page errors. Rubric: silently dead tap but visibly recoverable with an immediate retry, no data loss, no dead-end — S3 'janky-but-recoverable flow' fits; S2 would require the feature broken outright, which it is not.

Turn 2 (Ben): place anywhere wrong; Next player
Turn 3 (Ann): claim again, place correct, confirm both (Ann ->4, run 2); Next player

Read the reveal: yellow banner says 'Streak bonus - three in a row, +1 token' while the TOKENS ledger directly below says 'Ann  Streak bonus - tokens already full  0' and the pills stay at 5/5
confirmed.expected: When the cap swallows the streak payout, the banner must not assert '+1 token' - drop the payout clause or say tokens were full, matching the cap-honest ledger row
confirmed.actual: Banner is a static hardcoded string (index.html:1065) shown whenever outcome.streakAwarded is true (ui.js:3259), so at the cap the same screen simultaneously claims +1 and +0 for the same streak
sources: tokens-bets:Streak banner promises "+1 token" when the streak pays +0 at the token cap
confirmed.rationale: Single report. The underlying token math is correct (cap honored, ledger honest), so this is not a wrong game-rule outcome (S1) and no feature is broken (S2) - it is exactly the rubric's S3 'misleading copy', aggravated slightly by directly contradicting the ledger on the same reveal. Reporter's S3 stands.

v1.reason: Reproduced live in a fresh browser session (seed=777, 2 players, streak bonus ON, UI-only clicks). Ann: claim+correct+both votes on turns 1/3/5 with Ben placing wrong between; on turn 5 identify paid +1 (4->5, hitting the cap) and the streak completed in the same reveal. repro: Open https://music-timeline-walksalots-projects.vercel.app/listen.html# followed by base64url of {"v":1,"t":"The Ballad of the Extraordinarily Long Song Title","a":"Somebody & The Incredibly Verbose Backing Band","n":12} (any card whose preview cannot resolve)
Wait for resolution to fail: status shows "Couldn't stream this one. The links below will find it." and the links disclosure is surfaced
Read the footnote at the bottom of the page
confirmed.expected: Footnote matches the state via the existing per-state FOOTNOTES map, as listen.js already does for link mode and bad-payload notices
confirmed.actual: Footnote still reads 'Only the host's screen knows the year. Back to the game when the clip ends.' in the error state; stumble() never updates the footnote set by load() for player mode
sources: qr-listen:Listen page's stream-failure state keeps the footnote promise "Back to the game when the clip ends" although no clip will play in that state
confirmed.rationale: Separate defect from the disclosure-label finding: different element (footnote vs summary), different trigger (stream failure vs toggle), different code path (stumble() vs toggle handler) - so its own cluster. Impact is momentary confusion from a flavor-text footnote; the status line above it is honest. S4 wording polish, not S3 misleading copy, because the authoritative status message in the same view already tells the guest the truth. Reporter's S4 stands.

v1.reason: Reproduced live on first attempt with the exact reported steps: opened listen.html# + base64url of {"v":1,"t":"The Ballad of the Extraordinarily Long Song Title","a":"Somebody & The Incredibly Verbose Backing Band","n":12} on the production Vercel site; resolution failed to the non-retryable error state (status "Couldn't stream this one. The links below will find it.", links disclosure surfaced, body[data-state=error]) while #footnote still read "Only the host's screen knows the year. Back to the game when the clip ends." Code confirms the mechanism: load() sets FOOTNOTES.player (listen.js:548) and stumble() (listen.js:430-444) never updates the footnote, though showNotice() and link mode do swap it — contradicting the module's own comment that "each state gets the sentence it can keep," so it is not by design. Severity stays S4: the honest red status line directly above dominates the view, making this a wording inconsistency in muted flavor text, not S3 misleading copy. Evidence: scratch/qa/round-5/verify-listen-footnote-clip-ends-in-stream-failure-1/{verify.mjs,stream-failure-footnote.png}.

rejected.title: Double-tap on the pass screen's full-card 'Start the turn' target tap-throughs to the vinyl, drawing the card and starting the mystery song mid-handoff
rejected.reason: Ran the exact repro on the live site (fresh localStorage, seed=2026, touch double-tap 180ms and mouse 120ms) plus the control the reporter never ran: a SINGLE tap on #btn-pass-continue. The control alone produces the entire reported outcome — phase turn-start→listening, deck 1181→1180, audio src = audio-ssl.itunes.apple.com URL with an HTTP 206 fetch — identical state to both double-tap runs. The song starting and card drawing on the pass-screen tap is the app's default 'fast flow' feature (DEFAULT_SETTINGS.fastFlow: true, ui.js:211; handler comment at ui.js:4324 'Fast flow collapses the handoff to ONE tap ... draw the card AND start the song in the same tick'), and the live pass screen announces it in visible copy captured in my run and in the reporter's own screenshot (chaos/70-pass-before.png): 'Tap when only they can see the screen — the song starts right away.' So the finding's causal claim (second tap tap-throughs to the vinyl and causes the draw/song) is factually wrong — the second tap does land on #btn-play-song (confirmed via elementFromPoint) but causes none of the reported effects — and its 'expected' behavior (song waits for the vinyl tap) contradicts the app's stated, on-screen design. The reveal/setup 700ms guards cited as precedent protect transitions where a burst would do something unintended; here the tap's effect IS the intended action, so there is nothing to guard. The 'Playing the preview.' vs 'would not play here' status difference between runs is an artifact of this test box's missing AAC decoder (brief: not a finding). No incremental harm from the second tap beyond the vinyl's normal play/pause toggle. Not scored BY_DESIGN because the defect as stated (tap-through causes the song) is simply false, not merely intended: song start mid-handoff is first-tap designed behavior, reproduced 1-tap = 2-tap. Evidence: scratch/qa/round-5/verify-pass-screen-doubletap-starts-song-1/ (verify.mjs, A/B/C screenshots); zero console/page errors.
